title: CLAUDE.md
text: main exported functions maive() waive() (defined R/maivefunction.r), perform meta-analysis using instrumental variable estimation. functions share common pipeline via maive_run_pipeline(): Input Validation (normalize_maive_options): Validates normalizes input parameters resolves column mappings (estimate, se, n, optional study_id) Data Preparation (maive_prepare_data): Prepares study-level data, handles clustering fixed effects dummy matrix centering Variance Instrumentation (maive_compute_variance_instrumentation): First-stage regression variances inverse sample sizes, supporting levels log transformations Weighting (maive_compute_weights): Computes weights based weighting scheme (none, inverse-variance, MAIVE-adjusted, WAIVE) Shared Pipeline (maive_run_pipeline): Common second-stage analysis used maive() waive() Model Fitting (maive_fit_models): Fits PET (Precision-Effect Test), PEESE (Precision-Effect Estimate Standard Error), combined models Method Selection (maive_select_petpeese, maive_fit_ek): Selects PET/PEESE fits Endogenous Kink (EK) models Confidence Intervals (maive_compute_egger_ar_ci): Computes Anderson-Rubin confidence intervals weak instruments (handled R/ar.r) Bootstrap (R/boot.r): Wild cluster bootstrap standard errors SE=3

title: CLAUDE.md
text: maive() function expects data frame : Column 1: bs - Primary estimates Column 2: sebs - Standard errors (must > 0) Column 3: Ns - Sample sizes (must > 0) Column 4 (optional): study_id - Study identification clustering/fixed effects

title: CLAUDE.md
text: method: 1=PET, 2=PEESE, 3=PET-PEESE (default), 4=EK weight: 0=none (default), 1=inverse-variance, 2=MAIVE-adjusted instrument: 0=, 1=yes (default) - whether instrument standard errors studylevel: 0=none, 1=fixed effects, 2=cluster (default), 3=SE: 0=CR0 (Huber-White), 1=CR1, 2=CR2, 3=wild bootstrap (default) AR: 0=, 1=yes (default) - compute Anderson-Rubin CI (unweighted IV) first_stage: 1=log (default), 0=levels (published paper) - first-stage functional form Note: WAIVE available standalone waive() function provides aggressive correction p-hacking spurious precision downweighting spuriously precise estimates outliers.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: studylevel parameter encodes two dimensions via modular arithmetic: cluster = studylevel %/% 2 (integer division) dummy = studylevel %% 2 (modulo) Study fixed effects demeaned intercept measures grand mean. implemented via maive_center_dummy_matrix() centers dummy variables drops one column.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: AR CI computation (R/ar.r) uses adaptive grid search performance optimizations: Grid resolution adapts sample size parameter uncertainty Pre-computes projection matrices efficiency Disables AR datasets >5000 observations avoid memory issues Uses tighter bounds (2.5 standard errors) better performance available unweighted IV estimators

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Two functional forms instrumenting variances (sebs²): Log (first_stage=1, default): Log-linear regression smearing retransformation handle heteroskedasticity; fitted variance always positive Levels (first_stage=0): Linear regression sebs² constant 1/Ns; specification published paper levels fit can give negative fitted variance individual row. maive_apply_variance_exclusion() drops rows explicitly (flooring, see #24) weights, second stage, F-test (refit kept rows), Hausman, AR, bootstrap, warns count, returns n_excluded. log specification uses Duan’s smearing estimator retransform predictions back levels.

title: Getting Started with MAIVE
text: MAIVE (Meta-Analysis Instrumental Variable Estimator) addresses fundamental problem meta-analysis observational research: spurious precision. Traditional meta-analysis assigns weight studies lower standard errors, assuming higher precision. However, observational research, precision must estimated vulnerable manipulation practices like p-hacking achieve statistical significance. guided, interactive workflow, visit https://www.easymeta.org. manipulation can invalidate: Inverse-variance weighting schemes Bias-correction methods like funnel plots Traditional publication bias corrections MAIVE introduces instrumental variable approach limit bias caused spurious precision meta-analysis.

text: observational research, researchers can inadvertently deliberately manipulate analyses achieve statistically significant results. includes: Selective reporting specifications Outcome switching Sample trimming Selective controls inclusion practices create spuriously precise estimates appear reliable actually . title: Getting Started with MAIVE
text: maive() function returns list following key elements (see ?maive full list): beta: MAIVE point estimate (corrected spurious precision) SE: MAIVE standard error beta_standard, SE_standard: Conventional (non-IV) estimate standard error comparison Hausman: Hausman-type test comparing IV vs OLS estimates (high value suggests spurious precision) F-test: First-stage F-test instrument strength AR_CI: Anderson-Rubin confidence interval (robust weak instruments) pub bias p-value: p-value publication bias test based instrumented FAT SE_instrumented: Vector instrumented standard errors, one per input row (NA excluded estimates) n_excluded, excluded_rows: Number positions estimates excluded levels first stage fitted non-positive variance (0 integer(0) log first stage) petpeese_selected: PET PEESE selected method = 3 ek_structure: Structure EK fit method = 4 (“kink”, “linear”, “intercept”)

title: Subset Anderson-Rubin CI for the slope coefficient — compute_AR_CI_slope_only
text: method robust weak instruments avoids "banana projection" artifact can produce spuriously narrow CIs projecting 2D joint AR regions. Algorithm (per tjhavranek, Nov 2025): 1. candidate slope b1, form residuals: r_i = y_i - b1 * x_i 2. Run auxiliary regression: r ~ 1 + z (intercept absorbs b0) 3. Use cluster-robust (CR2) variance z coefficient 4. Test statistic: t_z^2 clustered test 5. Accept b1 t_z^2 <= qchisq(0.95, df = 1) = 3.84 References: - Guggenberger, P., Kleibergen, F. (2012). Econometrica. - Andrews, D. W. K., & Mikusheva, . (2016). Econometrica.
